A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same f-DMU research, with matching authors, core objectives and convergence theorems. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient measurements, qualitative generations, single- and multi-concept erasure experiments, and CS, CA and KID results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for further model configurations, ten-style erasure, nudity removal and adversarial robustness in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The target-to-anchor framework, closed-form objectives and variational minimax procedure remain. H-DMU and P-DMU rename existing instances. v2 supplies derivations for the alpha-divergence family already proposed in v1; additional architectures and implementation disclosures do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds nudity removal using the I2P nudity subset and MMA-Diffusion prompts, adversarial nudity and artistic-style scenarios using Ring-A-Bell, and a broader set of artists for sequential erasure. The earlier three-concept sequence remains in Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's MSE/Concept Ablation and divergence comparisons, v2 evaluates methods including ESD, SPM, UCE, MACE, RECE, SAFREE and SPEED, plus SLD in nudity experiments. Conversely, the corresponding 500-step comparison removes the MSE empty and MSE near rows from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 14.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce SD 1.5, SD 2.1, SDXL, SD3 and FLUX configurations and distinct protocols: 800-step closed-form nudity unlearning, 250-step transformer experiments and 50 steps per artistic style. Nudity-generation rates, body-region counts and adversarial-prompt evaluations supplement the retained CS, CA and KID evaluations.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of whether adversarial prompts recover erased nudity or Van Gogh style, including Tables 4 and 10 and Figure 14. It also adds body-region/gender breakdowns and a ten-style cumulative-erasure study. Earlier regularization and training-duration analyses remain, although some matching MSE anchor controls are removed.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly states that main results are averaged over multiple random seeds. Neither version supplies seed counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. This is additional reporting, without evidence that the number of runs increased.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive model, multi-style and nudity/attack results; Table 4, for example, reports I2P rates of 0.063 for H-DMU and 0.120 for CAbl. Most earlier SD 1.4 values remain. Table 14 removes MSE-anchor results and changes Van Gogh KID from -0.007 to 0.007 when erasing Snoopy with Hellinger near and both regularizers.

T1.justification: Appendices B.1.1–B.1.2 add alpha-divergence definitions, Gaussian formulas, variance conditions and a general gradient derivation, previously only promised. The main convergence theorems remain, while v1's variational-reformulation justification in Eqs. 49–50 is removed. The new general loss also leaves handling of the sign-sensitive normalization between v2 Eqs. 48–49 unexplained for alpha greater than one.

C1.justification: The central unification and local-convergence contributions remain. v2 explicitly extends its empirical superiority claim to nudity, singles out closed-form Hellinger as consistently dominating MSE in the abstract, and recommends it as the default in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds a small-batch divergence-estimation explanation for variational artifacts and distinguishes per-sample weighting from batch-level learning-rate adjustment. It expands practical loss-selection advice and states GPU-related limits on architecture testing. The existing aggressive-erasure versus preservation interpretation remains central.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and substantially expands optimizer, learning-rate, updated-parameter, discriminator warm-up, batch-size and prompt-source information. It newly discloses the larger prompt set used for retained ablation tables. However, v1's DDIM sampler and 30/50 inference-step specification disappears; these documentation changes do not establish reruns.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of GLoCE and references supporting newer models, adversarial benchmarks, SPEED and optimization comparisons. Its positioning of CAbl and DoCo as special cases, and its claim to a general f-divergence unlearning framework, remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, results narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and method-instance terminology is standardized. Sequential erasure is integrated into Section 5.3, while Appendix C is reorganized into dedicated architecture, multi-concept, nudity, robustness, comparison and ablation sections, redistributing existing explanations as well as accommodating additions.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column conference layout and adds numerous plots, image comparisons and tables with comparison highlighting. Existing Figures 1, 5 and 6 move to v2 Figures 16, 15 and 12; the earlier divergence-wheel diagram disappears. New alpha-gradient surfaces and nudity/robustness displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the framework's generality beyond v1's SD 1.4-centered evaluation through additional architectures, independent baselines, nudity/adversarial tests and quantitative multi-style erasure. Fuller implementation details also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed MSE-anchor controls, although the broad robustness claim conflicts with Table 4's Ring-A-Bell results and the new alpha objective has an unexplained sign-sensitive normalization in Eqs. 48–49.
